config.title: When Is Berlin Busiest - FAQ
config.subtitle: The trade fair and event windows that fill Berlin's hotels, what each one actually changes, and how far you have to move your dates.

items.a: **Berlin gets busy in short dated windows, not in one long season.** The heaviest are the trade fairs at Messe Berlin: IFA in early September, InnoTrans in late September every second year, Grüne Woche for ten days in January, and ITB in mid March. Add the marathon on the last Sunday of September, the Berlinale in February and New Year's Eve, and you have almost every week that matters. Summer and December are busy for the museums, but they do not move hotel prices the way a fair week does.

items.q: Do trade fairs make Berlin more expensive for tourists?
items.a: **Yes, and mostly through accommodation.** A fair like IFA brought around 220,000 visitors from 140 countries in 2025 and InnoTrans counted 169,214 in 2024, almost all of them sleeping in Berlin hotels. City West fills first because the grounds are in Charlottenburg, then demand rolls east into Mitte. Restaurants, museums and attractions are unaffected, so the extra cost lands on your room and nowhere else.

items.q: Which weeks should I avoid in Berlin?
items.a: **If you can move your dates, step around 4 to 8 September 2026 (IFA), 22 to 27 September 2026 (InnoTrans and the marathon), 30 December to 1 January, 15 to 24 January 2027 (Grüne Woche), 10 to 21 February 2027 (Berlinale) and 16 to 18 March 2027 (ITB).** Four or five days in either direction is normally enough, because these windows are short and they rarely run into each other.

items.q: Is the Berlin Marathon weekend a bad time to visit?
items.a: **It is a wonderful weekend and an awkward Sunday.** On 27 September 2026 the course runs through Mitte, Tiergarten, Kreuzberg and Charlottenburg and finishes at the Brandenburg Gate, with roads closed from early morning into the afternoon. The U-Bahn runs underneath and is the reliable way to cross the city. Buses and trams are diverted, so plan a walking day on one side of the route and stay on that side.

items.q: When is Berlin cheapest to visit?
items.a: **The first ten days of January and the second half of November, outside the market weekends.** January would be the clear winner if Grüne Woche did not occupy 15 to 24 January 2027 with ten public fair days. Early February before Fruit Logistica and the Berlinale is the other quiet stretch. February is cold and dark, which is exactly why the rooms are cheap.

items.q: Do I need to change my sightseeing plans during a Berlin trade fair?
items.a: **No.** The Messe grounds are out in Charlottenburg, 25 minutes from Alexanderplatz on the Ringbahn plus an S-Bahn. Nothing in the historic centre notices. Museum queues, restaurant tables and my free walking tour run exactly as they do in a quiet week. The only visible sign in the centre is more suitcases on the Ringbahn.

items.q: Which Berlin events do not have 2027 dates yet?
items.a: **CSD Berlin, Karneval der Kulturen, the DFB-Pokal final and the Formula E race.** CSD is traditionally the fourth Saturday of July, Karneval der Kulturen falls on the Whitsun weekend which in 2027 is 14 to 17 May, the cup final is usually a Saturday in late May at the Olympiastadion, and Formula E races on the old Tempelhof apron in spring. If your trip touches those months, check the organiser's own site before booking.
